investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T17:22–17:29Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past pod scheduling.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all concurrent or queued remote agent pods are competing for a finite pool of peer-pod VM slots that is currently at zero available.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes means the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes; any spike in demand or resource leak on those 2 nodes immediately exhausts capacity.
[Possible] A resource leak or stuck remote agent pod from a prior run is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new pods from being scheduled.

[Possible] The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been cordoned, drained, or had their extended resource advertisement reduced by the node agent (e.g., cloud-api-adaptor or peer-pods operator), shrinking available capacity to zero.

[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request quantity for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more slots than exist per node) could cause permanent unschedulability even on otherwise healthy nodes — but the message wording 'Insufficient' rather than 'resource limit exceeded' points more toward exhaustion than misconfiguration.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or invoking its runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod was left Unschedulable for 146 seconds before the check timed out. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that capacity exhaustion, not a software defect in the eval runner or contract definition, is the proximate cause. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and all three sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — Insufficient node pool size: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and match the pod's node affinity/selector. If baseline demand already saturates those 2 nodes, any new remote-agent pod will be immediately Unschedulable regardless of timing.

TERTIARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes. A recent node label change or taint addition could have reduced the eligible pool without changing the pod spec.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Leaked or un-cleaned eval pods from a prior run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) failed to release resources from a previous run, those slots would remain occupied. No cleanup-failure evidence is present in this packet.
